# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old by the end of Volume 4  <sub>[v2 c23 P6](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0006), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States (Boston)  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
- **Role:** Student and aspiring poet / writer  <sub>[v2 c15 P28](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0028), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), [v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has a delicate, refined, and exceptionally beautiful face framed in a halo of chestnut curls, which he later crops short as he grows older. He has big, dark blue eyes that match his father's, and an expressive, crimson-lipped mouth with a dimpled corner. Though small for his age during his early years in Avonlea, he eventually shoots up into a tall, handsome, and sturdy youth.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P8](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0008), [v2 c15 P27](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0027), [v2 c23 P24](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0024), [v2 c27 P27](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0027), [v2 c28 P9](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0009), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Paul is a highly imaginative, sensitive, and meditative boy who possesses a rare poetic soul and a deep appreciation for beauty. Though thoughtful, grave, and given to vivid daydreams about 'rock people' and fairies, he is also manly, good-tempered, and well-liked by his peers in school games. He is deeply affectionate and loyal, holding a reverent devotion to his late mother and a strong sense of duty toward his family.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c11 P42](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0042), [v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009), [v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020)_

## History

Paul Irving was born in the United States to Stephen Irving and his wife, who died when Paul was a small child. At ten years old, he was sent to Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving. He enrolled in Avonlea School, where he quickly formed an intense bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, recognizing her as a kindred spirit who understood his rich imaginary world of 'rock people.' When his father visited Avonlea, Paul helped reunite Stephen with his old love, Miss Lavendar Lewis, whom Paul warmly accepted as a second mother. Paul later moved to Boston with his father, Miss Lavendar, and Charlotta the Fourth. Over the years, he maintained a faithful correspondence with Anne and developed a talent for poetry, eventually publishing verses. At sixteen, he returned to the Island for a summer visit before going abroad to Europe for two years of study, attending Anne and Gilbert's wedding at Green Gables.

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright's field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because... I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> Grandma says father was brought up on porridge, and it certainly did work well in his case, for you ought to see the shoulders he has. But sometimes... I really think porridge will be the death of me.  <sub>[v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011)</sub>

> Isn't it splendid to be that kind, teacher?  <sub>[v2 c15 P19](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0019)</sub>

> Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.  <sub>[v2 c19 P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)</sub>

> You'll never grow old, Teacher. You are one of the fortunate mortals who have found and drunk from the Fountain of Youth—you and Mother Lavendar.  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
